description: Adds $128,900 to Water Conservation Capital Project P.02197.
Funding comes from NRCan and FCM grants.
Purchases new diesel and gas buses for Saskatoon Transit.
Funded by $23.5 million from city borrowing.

chips.text: Councillor Timon questioned the limited number of Access Transit buses.
Bus riders of Saskatoon endorse the plan but note past fleet neglect.
Access Transit users face long waits and missed appointments.
Public letters expressed disappointment over fossil fuel reliance for new buses.
Staff promised a Q2 fleet renewal plan addressing growth and demand.

description: Permits shared e-scooters on public right-of-way.
City will select up to two e-scooter vendors.
Bylaw 7200 will be amended for e-scooter operation.

chips.text: Councillor Ford questioned low bylaw enforcement (4 tickets in two years).
Local businesses benefited from $5.6 million in e-scooter rider spending.
City Solicitor noted the limited permit process was unusual for the city.
Administration did not know why few companies applied for e-scooter permits.
Councillor Pearce flagged a $5,000 vehicle damage claim denied by Neuron Mobility.
Disabled residents reported scooters blocking access on sidewalks and crosswalks.
Neuron stated about half of e-scooter trips replace car journeys.
Neuron Mobility offered to engage with the Accessibility Advisory Committee.

description: Retains McKercher Drive extension possibility to Berini Drive.
Allocates land for McKercher Drive and 105th Street intersection.
Offers land to Muskeg Lake Cree Nation; places proceeds into reserve.

chips.text: Councillor Jeffries argued to retain extension for future city development.
Council retained extension possibility despite staff traffic modeling.
Bus Riders of Saskatoon opposed abandoning extension, citing transit impacts.
Councillor Pearce opposed due to lack of public engagement and permanent land sale.
Muskeg Lake Cree Nation offered adjacent Parcel B land for sale.
